question: Can free-form, open-ended visual question answering serve as an automatically evaluable AI-complete task, and how hard is a large human-written dataset for it?
hypothesis: Answering open-ended questions about images needs more detailed image understanding and commonsense reasoning than image captioning, so captions or language alone are not enough.
contributions: Define the free-form open-ended and multiple-choice VQA tasks
Release a dataset of ~0.25M images, ~0.76M questions, ~10M answers (real COCO images and abstract scenes)
Analyse questions, answers, commonsense need, and captions vs questions
Provide baselines and an LSTM+CNN model compared with human performance
Set up an evaluation server, leaderboard, annual challenge

method.summary: Crowdsourced (AMT) questions written to stump a 'smart robot' for 204,721 COCO images and 50,000 abstract scenes, 3 questions each, 10 human answers each. Baselines and a two-channel model (frozen VGGNet fc7 image features + LSTM question embedding, fused by element-wise product, MLP softmax over top-1000 answers) are scored against humans.
method.task: visual question answering (open-ended and 18-way multiple choice)

datasets.name: VQA real images (MS COCO)
datasets.size: 204,721 images (123,287 train/val + 81,434 test); 614,163 questions; 7,984,119 answers (incl. no-image answers). Train+val 369,861 questions
datasets.split: COCO train/val/test; test-dev, test-standard, test-challenge, test-reserve
datasets.preprocessing: Answers lowercased, numbers to digits, punctuation and articles removed before comparison

datasets.name: VQA abstract scenes
datasets.source: clipart scenes built by AMT workers (20 paperdoll humans, 100+ objects, 31 animals)

datasets.name: Filtered VQA train+val (ablation)
datasets.source: Only answers with subject confidence 'yes'; questions with >=5/10 such answers; 8.77 answers/question

models.name: deeper LSTM Q + norm I
models.architecture: VGGNet fc7 (4096-d, l2-normalised, frozen) -> FC+tanh to 1024; 2-layer LSTM (512 cell+hidden per layer, 2048-d) -> FC+tanh to 1024; element-wise multiply; MLP 2 hidden layers x 1000 units, tanh, dropout 0.5; softmax over K=1000
models.init_from: VGGNet ImageNet classification weights, not fine-tuned

models.name: LSTM Q + I
models.architecture: 1-layer LSTM, 1024-d question embedding (512 cell + 512 hidden), un-normalised I

models.name: BoW Q + I
models.architecture: 1,030-d bag of words (top 1,000 words + 30-d first/second/third word) concatenated with I

models.name: random, prior (yes), per Q-type prior, nearest neighbor
models.architecture: non-learned/lookup baselines; nearest neighbor uses Skip-Thought question similarity then caffenet fc7 image similarity, k=4

training.objective: cross-entropy over K=1000 answers, end-to-end except VGGNet

other.train_data: VQA train+val (captions variants: train only, tested on val)

inference.decoding: open-ended: highest-activation of K answers; multiple-choice: highest activation among the 18 candidates
inference.samples: single run per model, no seeds reported

metrics.name: VQA accuracy
metrics.definition: min(# humans that provided that answer / 3, 1), averaged over all 10-choose-9 subsets of human annotators; exact string match after normalisation

metrics.name: multiple-choice accuracy
metrics.definition: same metric on the chosen option among 18 candidates (correct, plausible x3, 10 popular, random)

eval.protocol: Machine accuracies on test-dev, final on test-standard via evaluation server; human accuracy on test-standard; caption variants on val. No significance testing or repeated runs for model scores.

availability.code: CloudCV demo http://cloudcv.org/vqa; annotation UI at https://github.com/tylin/coco-ui

prompts.purpose: Question-collection instruction shown to AMT workers
prompts.text: We have built a smart robot. It understands a lot about images. It can recognize and name all the objects, it knows where the objects are, it can recognize the scene (e.g., kitchen, beach), people’s expressions and poses, and properties of objects (e.g., color of objects, their texture). Your task is to stump this smart robot! Ask a question about this scene that this smart robot probably can not answer, but any human can easily answer while looking at the scene in the image.

limits: Training hyperparameters (optimizer, learning rate, batch size, epochs, hardware) are not stated.
Language-only models reach 48.76% open-ended, so the benchmark rewards question priors; authors cite Zhang et al. (Yin and Yang) on biases.
Exact-string-match accuracy ignores synonyms and plurals, depressing 'other' agreement (<76%).
Age and commonsense estimates reflect MTurk perception, not true requirements.
Answers are mostly one word (89.32%), so the task is short-answer only.
Dated: models are 2015-era VGG+LSTM; scores superseded.

terms.definition: an answer is deemed 100% accurate if at least 3 workers provided that exact answer
test-dev for debugging with unlimited submissions; test-standard the default for reporting; test-reserve guards against overfitting; test-challenge decides winners
